# Distillation of the Semiformal Concept Set

Working document. The goal is to reduce twenty-one candidate concepts to the core
of the core by mapping their relations, finding overlaps and level mismatches, and
iterating until the whole design space is legible. The final catalog lives in
`semiformal-concepts.md`. This document records how the set was reached.

## The twenty-one candidates

Specification. Slot, Inert Marker, Intent Medium, Template and Arguments, Intent
Identity.

Commitment. Commitment Time, Use as Oracle, Resolution Choice, Deferred Freeze,
Earned Abstraction.

Evolution. Commitment History, Divergence Signal, Escalating Doubt, Behavioral
Memory, Measured Change, Reified Effects.

Elicitation. Two Pens, Inference Surface, Choice Surface, Promotion, Two Users.

## Edge types used in the graph

- subsumes. A is general, B is a special case of A.
- serves. B is a mechanism in service of A.
- seam. A and B are the two sides of one boundary the design has to draw.
- entangled. A and B co-define each other and both earn a place.
- level. B is a tactic or dimension sitting one abstraction below A.

## Iteration 0. The full graph

```mermaid
graph TD
  Slot[Slot]
  Marker[Inert Marker]
  Medium[Intent Medium]
  TA[Template and Arguments]
  Ident[Intent Identity]
  CTime[Commitment Time]
  Oracle[Use as Oracle]
  Res[Resolution Choice]
  Freeze[Deferred Freeze]
  Abstr[Earned Abstraction]
  Hist[Commitment History]
  Diverge[Divergence Signal]
  Doubt[Escalating Doubt]
  Mem[Behavioral Memory]
  Change[Measured Change]
  Fx[Reified Effects]
  Pens[Two Pens]
  Surface[Inference Surface]
  Choice[Choice Surface]
  Promote[Promotion]
  Users[Two Users]

  Marker -->|level| Slot
  Medium -->|level| Slot
  TA -->|seam| Slot
  TA -->|serves| Ident
  TA -->|serves| Oracle
  Ident -->|serves| Hist
  Ident -->|serves| Res
  CTime -->|entangled| Oracle
  Oracle -->|serves| Res
  Freeze -->|subsumes-under| CTime
  Freeze -->|serves| Res
  Abstr -->|subsumes-under| Res
  Res -->|entangled| Hist
  Diverge -->|serves| Res
  Diverge -->|entangled| Doubt
  Doubt -->|level| Diverge
  Mem -->|entangled| Diverge
  Change -->|subsumes-under| Mem
  Ident -->|governs| Mem
  Fx -->|serves| Res
  Pens -->|entangled| Surface
  Choice -->|subsumes-under| Surface
  Promote -->|operates-on| Pens
  Promote -->|governs| Ident
  Pens -->|constrained-by| Ident
  Users -.lens.-> Slot
```

Reading the graph, four things are visible immediately.

Some nodes sit a level below a neighbour and are tactics, not concepts. Inert Marker
and Intent Medium are dimensions of Slot. Escalating Doubt is a cost tactic under
Divergence Signal. Measured Change is one mechanism inside Behavioral Memory. Choice
Surface is a kind of Inference Surface. Deferred Freeze is a policy for choosing
Commitment Time. Earned Abstraction is one mode of Resolution Choice.

Some pairs are entangled and both earn a place. Commitment Time and Use as Oracle
co-define, since late timing exists so that use can supply evidence. Divergence
Signal and Behavioral Memory co-define, since the contract's checks are the very
signals that flag divergence. Two Pens and Inference Surface co-define the writing
surface.

Some nodes are hubs. Resolution Choice consumes Identity, Divergence, History, and
evidence. Intent Identity is consumed by History, Resolution, Memory, and Promotion.

One node is a different kind of thing. Two Users is a framing lens over the whole
graph, not a mechanism inside it.

## Iteration 1. Fold the tactics and special cases into their parents

- Inert Marker, Intent Medium fold into Slot.
- Escalating Doubt folds into Divergence Signal.
- Measured Change folds into Behavioral Memory.
- Choice Surface folds into Inference Surface.
- Deferred Freeze folds into Commitment Time.
- Earned Abstraction folds into Resolution Choice.

Remaining nodes, fifteen. Slot, Template and Arguments, Intent Identity, Commitment
Time, Use as Oracle, Resolution Choice, Commitment History, Divergence Signal,
Behavioral Memory, Reified Effects, Two Pens, Inference Surface, Promotion, Two
Users.

## Iteration 2. Merge the co-defining pairs into single concepts

- Commitment Time plus Use as Oracle become one concept, Deferred Commitment. Timing
  and evidence are two faces of one decision, to commit at use so that use supplies
  the evidence.
- Divergence Signal plus Behavioral Memory stay distinct after a hard look. Divergence
  is checking one mechanism against the current input. Memory is carrying reasons and
  constraints across regenerations. They meet, since a contract check is a divergence
  test, and the shared machinery is real, yet they answer different questions. The
  entanglement is kept and named instead of merged.
- Two Pens plus Inference Surface plus Promotion collapse into one concept, Gradual
  Formalization. The dual channel and the surfaced inference exist so that a human can
  promote an inference into a commitment. The mechanism only means something as a
  whole.
- Reified Effects generalizes into Trusted Effect Gate, the principle that an
  untrusted mechanism's consequences pass through a trusted inspectable layer before
  reaching the world.

Remaining, ten. Slot, Template and Arguments, Intent Identity, Deferred Commitment,
Resolution Choice, Commitment History, Divergence Signal, Behavioral Memory, Trusted
Effect Gate, Gradual Formalization. Plus Two Users as a lens.

## Iteration 3. Sort the ten into abstraction levels

Writing the ten on one line hides that they are not peers. They stack.

- Substrate, what gets committed. Slot. Template and Arguments is the seam inside the
  slot between durable intent and transient evidence, so it is a facet of Slot rather
  than a peer.
- The act, how intent turns into mechanism. Deferred Commitment.
- Management of a commitment over time. Intent Identity, Commitment History,
  Resolution Choice, Behavioral Memory. Divergence Signal is the verification step
  inside Resolution and inside Memory, so it drops as a peer and lives inside both.
- Interfaces, where the informal program meets a human and the world. Gradual
  Formalization, Trusted Effect Gate.
- Lens over all layers. Two Users.

Folding Template and Arguments into Slot and Divergence Signal into Resolution and
Memory leaves eight mechanism concepts plus one lens.

## Iteration 4. Test each survivor for definitional necessity and settle the core

The test is whether removing the concept turns semiformal programming back into
ordinary programming or into a bare model call.

- Slot. Removing it removes partial specification. Definitional.
- Deferred Commitment. Removing it commits everything up front, which is ordinary
  programming. Definitional.
- Intent Identity. Removing it regenerates on every call, which is a chatbot in a
  loop. Definitional, and it is the hub the other management concepts hinge on.
- Resolution Choice. Removing it freezes the first mechanism forever, which is a
  cache over one model call. Definitional, since evolution is the claim.
- Behavioral Contract, the renamed Behavioral Memory. Removing it lets evolution
  regress in silence. Definitional for a system meant to be trusted.
- Gradual Formalization. Removing it removes the dial between informal and formal,
  which is the semi in semiformal. Definitional.
- Commitment History. Removing it keeps a working system that cannot roll back or
  audit its own autonomous edits. Important, and it is the store that Resolution and
  Contract operate on, so it reads as the substrate of the management layer more than
  an independent claim. Second ring.
- Trusted Effect Gate. Removing it is fine for pure functions and only matters once
  the program acts on the world. An extension for a class of programs. Second ring.

The definitional core is six. Slot, Deferred Commitment, Intent Identity, Resolution
Choice, Behavioral Contract, Gradual Formalization. Two second-ring concepts extend
it, Commitment History as the store beneath the management layer, and Trusted Effect
Gate as the world-facing boundary. Two Users stays a lens.

Key entanglements to state rather than dissolve. Intent Identity is the hub, since a
change of intent mints a new identity, which retires the contract, opens a fresh
history, and is exactly what Promotion triggers. Resolution and History are two
halves of one act, the decision and the store it reads and writes. Divergence lives
inside both Resolution and Contract as the shared act of checking.

Drafting of the six core writeups now proceeds in `semiformal-concepts.md`, after
which one last pass revisits the boundaries that writing exposes.

## Iteration 5. Adjustments the writing forced

Recorded after the core writeups were drafted.

- Writing Deferred Commitment and Resolution Choice back to back showed the first
  commitment is the generate branch of resolution under a deferral policy. The clean
  division holds once each concept is scoped tightly. Deferred Commitment owns the
  question of when a mechanism is born and on what evidence. Resolution Choice owns
  the recurring question of what to do when a mechanism already exists. The word
  commit was removed from Resolution to stop the two blurring.
- Writing Intent Identity pulled the Template and Arguments seam back up to near
  peer status inside the entry, since the sameness of two slots is unstatable until
  the durable intent is separated from the transient values. It stays inside Slot as
  a concept and is invoked in Identity, and both entries now name the seam explicitly.
- Writing Behavioral Contract and Commitment History side by side confirmed they are
  two memories with different jobs, one of mechanisms and their lineage, one of
  constraints and their reasons. History earned a fuller treatment than second ring
  first suggested, so it is drafted at core depth and marked as the substrate of the
  management layer.
- Gradual Formalization absorbed Choice Surface cleanly, since a surfaced open
  decision and a surfaced inference are the same move with a different payload.

Final set. Six definitional concepts, two extending concepts, one lens. The catalog
presents all of them at depth, grouped by the layers found in Iteration 3.

# Semiformal Concepts

A catalog of the core design concepts of semiformal programming, reached by mapping
a larger candidate set down to the concepts that carry weight and cannot be reduced
into one another. The reduction is recorded in `semiformal-concepts-distillation.md`.
Six concepts are definitional, in the sense that removing any one turns the paradigm
back into ordinary programming or into a bare sequence of model calls. Two more
extend the core, one beneath it as the store the others operate on, one beside it as
the boundary to the world. A final lens colours every concept.

Each entry states the reflection that only becomes clear after building such a
system, then the move a sound design makes, then the symptom that reveals a wrong
choice.

## The design space in layers

The concepts are not peers. They stack, and reading them on one line hides that.

- Substrate, what gets committed. Slot.
- The act, how intent becomes a mechanism. Deferred Commitment.
- Management of a commitment over time. Intent Identity, Commitment History,
  Resolution Choice, Behavioral Contract.
- Interfaces, where the informal program meets a human and the world. Gradual
  Formalization, Trusted Effect Gate.
- Lens over all layers. Two Users.

```mermaid
graph TD
  Slot[Slot] --> DC[Deferred Commitment]
  DC --> Ident[Intent Identity]
  Ident -->|hub| Hist[Commitment History]
  Ident -->|hub| Res[Resolution Choice]
  Ident -->|hub| Contract[Behavioral Contract]
  Res <-->|decision and store| Hist
  Res -.shared check.- Contract
  Promote((Gradual Formalization)) -->|promotion mints identity| Ident
  Res --> Fx[Trusted Effect Gate]
  Users{{Two Users}} -.lens.- Slot
```

Intent Identity is the hub of the management layer. A change of intent mints a new
identity, which retires the contract, opens a fresh history, and is exactly the event
that promotion triggers. Resolution Choice and Commitment History are two halves of
one act, the decision and the store it reads and writes. The act of checking whether
a mechanism still holds lives inside both Resolution Choice and Behavioral Contract,
which is why the two are drawn as sharing it rather than owning it separately.

---

## Substrate

### Slot

A slot is a region of a program whose intent is written down and whose mechanism is
left open. The first design decision is how much of a program is allowed to be a
slot, an expression, a statement, a whole function, a type, or a whole module, since
a wider grammar of holes lets more of a program stay informal while making it harder
to state what each hole is obligated to return. Two dimensions live inside the slot.
The medium of the intent, whether prose, examples, a type, or an image, fixes some
aspects of the goal and leaves the rest open, and a richer medium draws out a better
mechanism while making two intents harder to compare for sameness. The embedding of
the slot in the host language decides whether an unfilled program still parses and
runs, since a marker the host already discards keeps a half written program alive
while a marker that breaks the parser blocks gradual adoption. A slot also carries a
seam between the durable intent and the transient values that flow through it at
runtime, and where that seam falls decides what counts as the same request with
different data. A sound design widens the grammar of holes only as far as it can
still name each hole's obligation, expresses intent in the smallest medium that pins
the goal, embeds slots with a marker the host ignores, and places the intent and
evidence seam so that data variation never reads as intent variation. A program that
stops parsing before every hole is filled has chosen an embedding that blocks
incremental work. A slot whose obligation cannot be stated has been allowed to span
more than the design can later verify.

---

## The act

### Deferred Commitment

Ordinary programs fix every mechanism before they run, and the defining move of the
paradigm postpones the mechanism of a slot until the moment it is first reached with
real data. The reason is evidence. A mechanism written in advance handles inputs the
author guessed at, while a mechanism written at first use is shaped by the values
actually present, and the shape of those values specifies the task more sharply than
most authors manage from imagination. Timing and evidence are one decision seen from
two sides, since the only reason to commit late is to let use supply the evidence,
and the amount of surrounding evidence gathered before committing, one value, a whole
column, the caller's context, sets how well the first mechanism generalizes. Some
slots resist any fixed mechanism, and whether a given slot is compilable at all is
discovered empirically by letting it run interpreted and freezing it into fixed code
only once it reproduces cases it was never shown. A sound design defers each slot's
mechanism to first use, gathers as much real evidence as the call site affords before
committing, and treats the freeze into fixed code as an empirical event licensed by
held out generalization instead of a declaration made in advance. A slot frozen on
its single first example tends to overfit and fail the second input. A slot that
never reproduces held out cases and is frozen regardless is one the design mistook
for compilable.

---

## Management of a commitment over time

### Intent Identity

Deciding when the system regards two slots as the same thing looks like a hashing
detail and operates as the rule that defines what an edit costs. Identity encodes a
standing promise about which edits preserve what the system has learned and which
discard it, and a developer's sense that the tool behaves reasonably rests on that
promise. Identity keyed on physical location discards a working mechanism the moment
a line moves, which reads as arbitrary to the person editing. Identity grounded in
the authored intent matches ordinary intuition, since rewording a request changes the
promise while reformatting the surrounding code leaves it intact. Stating sameness at
all requires the intent and evidence seam from the slot, because two slots can be the
same request only once the durable intent is separated from the transient values.
One further property surfaces after real use. Two identities do two jobs, one that
pins a slot to its own history in a single place, and one that lets two slots that
mean the same thing share a single mechanism across files. A last hazard arrives once
the system writes its inferences back into the source, since those machine lines have
to stay outside identity, or annotating a slot changes it and the annotation repeats
without end. A sound design grounds identity in the human's intent scoped to its
enclosing structure, drops everything positional, keeps a second location free key
over meaning and shape so equivalent intents share work, and excludes machine written
lines from both. A developer who reformats code and loses a mechanism has watched
position leak into identity. The same request in two files paying full generation
cost twice shows that no meaning level key exists.

### Commitment History

Treating generated code as a cache entry invites overwriting it on every change,
which throws away the record of what the system attempted and why it moved on. The
durable object worth keeping is a trail of decisions, and that trail is what licenses
an autonomous system to alter its own behavior, since it supports rolling back a poor
automatic edit and demonstrating that nothing regressed in silence. The fork and the
step form the subtle distinction. A step is the same approach corrected, superseding
what came before. A fork is a materially different approach retained in parallel
because either might prove right, one mechanism suited to one input shape and another
to a second. A design that misses the distinction either flattens away useful
alternatives or fills with dead branches. A further rule emerges once the system runs
unattended, that retired mechanisms stay in the record and stay marked, because a
deliberate change of mind and a silent regression have to occupy different and
visible states. A sound design fixes one rule for which mechanism counts as active
when several coexist and treats that rule as the single source of truth, branches on
adaptation so a correction never destroys the mechanism it corrected, and preserves
every superseded mechanism together with the reason it left service. Inability to
reconstruct, from the record alone, why a slot produces one output today and produced
another last week shows that the structure has become a cache with no genuine
history.

### Resolution Choice

Once a mechanism exists for a slot, every later call faces a choice among reusing it,
adapting it, and rewriting it, and the tempting reduction of that choice to a cache
hit or a regeneration is what makes naive systems thrash, since every correction then
discards everything the previous mechanism had learned and competence oscillates
instead of accumulating. The middle option carries the weight. Adaptation hands a
mechanism its own failing case and converts a run of failures into a converging
mechanism, where reuse and rewrite alone can only keep or discard. The choice has to
be one ordered rule applied the same way on every call, because an ad hoc choice
produces nondeterminism a developer cannot reproduce, with one slot behaving
differently across runs that appear identical. Seen from a distance, evidence drives
the choice. Adaptation fits a specific new input that has failed, rewrite fits the
case where nothing prior is worth keeping, and reuse fits evidence that matches
evidence already handled, and even reuse stays a hypothesis the system confirms
against the real input before returning it. A sound design expresses the choice as
one ordered function, defaults to adaptation whenever a mechanism exists and fails,
reserves rewrite for a changed specification or a mechanism worth abandoning, and
re-verifies every reuse on the actual input with checks ordered cheap before
expensive so the common case costs almost nothing. A slot that flips between two
implementations across identical runs signals rewriting where adaptation belonged. A
slot that serves visibly stale output signals reuse without re-verification.

### Behavioral Contract

The defining hazard of a system that rewrites itself is regression by omission, where
a fix for one input breaks another because the new mechanism never learned that the
other mattered. A conventional test suite assumes known expected outputs, and
informal intent rarely supplies them, since nothing states what a request to
summarize a passage ought to return. The workable response asserts the properties an
answer must hold and the relations it must obey, among them a non-empty result for
non-empty input, invariance under added whitespace, or membership in a fixed set of
labels, and such assertions survive a rewrite that phrases the answer differently
where a pinned pair of input and output would raise a false alarm. The deeper role is
memory. Carrying the reason behind each past decision into the next rewrite, so the
next generation learns that a mechanism exists because one format once failed, does
more work than the check itself, because that reason keeps the system from circling
back over ground it already covered. A sound design accumulates properties and
relations for each slot, pins exact examples only for small canonical output spaces,
feeds the reason a failed check exists into the rewrite, and seeds each check from the
current mechanism's own behavior so it holds the moment it is written. Checks that
fire on correct answers worded differently reveal examples pinned where properties
belonged. A fix that silently moved a valued output reveals a memory too thin to
defend it.

---

## Interfaces

### Gradual Formalization

The word semi in semiformal names a dial, and the human loop turns it from informal
toward formal one decision at a time. The source carries two kinds of writing, the
commitments a human owns and the inferences the system proposes, and the two stay in
separate visibly distinct channels so that authorship of any line is never in doubt.
The machine channel stays outside the slot's identity, since an inference written
beside a slot must not change what the slot is, and a system that re-derived identity
from its own annotations would annotate without end. What the system surfaces is held
to a small fixed vocabulary a human can scan, the assumed input shape, the strategy,
the fallback, what has been verified, and any open decision the evidence cannot
settle, while anything already visible in the code is dropped so the surface stays
worth reading. The loop closes with promotion, where a human rewrites an inference
they endorse as their own commitment, which changes the intent, mints a new identity,
and hands the system a hard requirement to defend from then on. A sound design gives
the human and the machine disjoint channels, keeps the machine channel identity
neutral, surfaces inferences and open forks in a closed vocabulary that earns each
line, and offers one gesture that promotes an inference into a commitment. A surface
no one reads has failed the earn its line test. A promotion that fails to raise the
system's obligation shows the loop between inference and commitment is broken.

### Trusted Effect Gate

A generated mechanism is not trusted, and the stakes rise when its output is an
action on the world rather than a value, since a wrong value can be checked and
discarded while a wrong deletion cannot be recalled. The response keeps the mechanism
from acting directly and has it describe the intended action as inspectable data that
a trusted layer, written by hand and never generated, reviews before anything takes
effect. That layer rehearses the action against a faithful copy so the mechanism can
branch on real state without risk, bounds the damage the action could do, and applies
it only under approval, all or nothing across a batch. Reversibility divides the
field. For an action with an inverse the layer captures the exact inverse at the
moment of acting and stores it, so undo replays what was done instead of re-deriving
it from code that may since have changed. For an action with no inverse the design
substitutes idempotency and an explicit human gate for the missing undo. A sound
design routes every world touching action through reified data and a trusted reviewer,
proves or bounds its blast radius before it fires, and records a captured inverse for
anything it intends to be able to revert. An effect that fired straight from generated
code has bypassed the gate. A revert that recomputes its inverse from the current
mechanism can undo something other than what it did.

---

## Lens

### Two Users

A semiformal system serves two audiences whose needs pull in opposite directions, the
developer who authors intent and the person who consumes the artifact the program
produces. The developer wants a surface that is live, forgiving, and promotable, one
that shows its inferences and absorbs correction. The consumer wants the opposite, a
mechanism that is stable, readable, and trustworthy without any knowledge of the
apparatus that produced it. The reconciling test is whether the consumer can read and
rely on the output while trusting nothing about the generator, which holds only when
the produced mechanism stays ordinary inspectable code carrying its own evidence of
verification. A design that meets the developer's need for fluidity by making the
output an opaque model call has failed the consumer. A design that meets the
consumer's need for stability by freezing the developer's surface has failed the
author. The lens applies to every other concept, since each is read once by the
author while writing and once by the consumer through the artifact it leaves behind.

# Semiformal Concepts as Design Guidelines

This document presents the core concepts of semiformal programming as a set of design
guidelines, each stated as a principle, grounded in prior work, and closed by the
symptom that reveals a wrong choice. The concepts and the reduction that produced them
are recorded in `semiformal-concepts-distillation.md`; here they are laid out the way
Shipman and Marshall laid out approaches to the problems of formalisms, as guidance a
designer can act on rather than an architecture to copy (Shipman & Marshall, 1999).

## The guidelines

Building a system that keeps part of a program informal has no single remedy. The nine
concepts below function as guidelines, each answering one recurring pressure and each
anchored in a line of prior work. Six are definitional, in that removing any one returns
the paradigm to ordinary programming or to a bare sequence of model calls. Three extend
the core, one beneath it as the store the others read, one beside it as the boundary to
the world, and one as a lens over all of them.

1. Keep the hole a first-class element of the host language rather than a string handed
   to a generator.
2. Defer the mechanism of a hole to first use and let runtime evidence shape it.
3. Ground the identity of a hole in its intent rather than its position.
4. Keep the record of past commitments as a navigable history rather than a cache.
5. Treat every later encounter with a resolved hole as an ordered choice among reuse,
   adaptation, and rewrite.
6. Defend behavior across rewrites with properties and remembered reasons rather than
   fixed expected outputs.
7. Move each hole from informal toward formal one endorsed decision at a time.
8. Route any effect on the world through an inspectable, trusted layer.
9. Design every mechanism for two readers at once, the author of intent and the consumer
   of the artifact.

## The design space in layers

The nine are not peers. They stack, and reading them on one line hides that.

```mermaid
graph TD
  Slot[1 Slot] --> DC[2 Deferred Commitment]
  DC --> Ident[3 Intent Identity]
  Ident -->|hub| Hist[4 Commitment History]
  Ident -->|hub| Res[5 Resolution Choice]
  Ident -->|hub| Contract[6 Behavioral Contract]
  Res <-->|decision and store| Hist
  Res -.shared check.- Contract
  Promote((7 Gradual Formalization)) -->|promotion mints identity| Ident
  Mech[resolved mechanism] --> Fx[8 Trusted Effect Gate]
  Users{{9 Two Users}} -.lens.- Slot
```

Substrate is what gets committed, guideline 1. The act is how intent turns into a
mechanism, guideline 2. Management of a commitment over time holds guidelines 3 through
6, with Intent Identity as the hub, since a change of intent mints a new identity, which
retires the contract, opens a fresh history, and is exactly what promotion triggers.
Resolution Choice and Commitment History are two halves of one act, the decision and the
store it reads and writes. The check that a mechanism still holds lives inside both
Resolution Choice and Behavioral Contract. Interfaces are where the informal program
meets a human and the world, guidelines 7 and 8. Guideline 9 is a lens over all of them.

---

## Substrate

### 1. Keep the hole first-class in the host (Slot)

Every system that leaves part of a program unwritten has to decide what a hole is and how
much of a program one may span. Typed holes in Hazel preserve well-typedness around a
missing subexpression so an incomplete program stays analyzable and runnable (Omar et
al., 2017), and program sketching lets a programmer leave holes for a solver to fill
(Solar-Lezama, 2009). Both treat the hole as a construct the language understands, which
is what keeps a half-written program alive. The width of the grammar of holes trades
reach against verifiability, since the more of a program that may stay informal the harder
it becomes to state what each hole must return, a tension visible in the move from
expression-level holes to whole natural-language specifications, where formalizing the
language tends to reproduce the rigidity it was meant to escape (Dijkstra, 1979; Sammet,
1966) and the resulting abstraction can conceal the decisions that most need attention
(Steimann, 2018). Two dimensions sit inside the hole. The medium of the intent, whether
prose, examples, a type, or handwritten notation, fixes some of the goal and leaves the
rest open, and richer media draw out a better mechanism while making two intents harder
to compare (Green, 1989; Arawjo et al., 2022; Lindenbaum et al., 2022). The embedding in
the host decides whether an unfilled program still parses, which is why a marker the host
already discards keeps incremental work possible. A sound design widens the grammar of
holes only as far as it can still name each hole's obligation, expresses intent in the
smallest medium that pins the goal, and embeds the hole with a marker the host ignores. A
program that stops parsing before every hole is filled has chosen an embedding that blocks
incremental adoption. A hole whose obligation cannot be stated has been allowed to span
more than the design can later verify.

---

## The act

### 2. Defer the mechanism to first use (Deferred Commitment)

Ordinary programs fix every mechanism before they run, and the defining move of the
paradigm postpones the mechanism of a hole until it is first reached with real data, the
strategy named directly in Thimbleby's account of delaying commitment (Thimbleby, 1988)
and motivated by the observation that the distinctions a program must draw often surface
only at runtime (Petricek, 2021). The reason is evidence. A mechanism written in advance
handles inputs the author imagined, while a mechanism written at first use is shaped by
the values actually present, the same principle that lets program-by-example systems infer
a transformation from concrete demonstrations (Gulwani, 2011; Wang et al., 2021) and lets
library-learning systems grow abstractions from observed programs (Ellis et al., 2021).
Timing and evidence are one decision seen from two sides, since the only reason to commit
late is to let use supply the evidence, and the amount of surrounding context gathered
before committing sets how well the first mechanism generalizes. This late commitment
separates the paradigm from declarative frameworks that keep a prompt in source but
re-execute it at every invocation (Khattab et al., 2023; Beurer-Kellner et al., 2023;
Zheng et al., 2024), where the specification is consumed anew each call rather than
committed once to a durable artifact. Some holes resist any fixed mechanism, and whether a
hole is compilable at all is discovered empirically by running it interpreted and freezing
it into fixed code only once it reproduces cases it was never shown. A sound design defers
each hole's mechanism to first use, gathers as much real evidence as the call site
affords, and treats the freeze into fixed code as an empirical event licensed by held out
generalization. A hole frozen on its single first example tends to overfit the second
input. A hole that never reproduces held out cases and is frozen regardless is one the
design mistook for compilable.

---

## Management of a commitment over time

### 3. Ground identity in intent (Intent Identity)

Deciding when two holes are the same thing looks like a hashing detail and operates as the
rule that sets what an edit costs. Content-addressed identity, where a value is named by a
hash of what it contains (Merkle, 1987), gives a stable handle, and the design choice is
what to feed the hash. Identity keyed on physical location discards a working mechanism
the moment a line moves, which reads as arbitrary to the person editing, while identity
grounded in the authored intent matches the sense that reformatting leaves a program's
meaning intact, a view of the program as an evolving theory held by its author (Naur,
1985). Two identities do two jobs, one that pins a hole to its own history in a single
place, and one keyed over meaning and shape so that two holes expressing the same intent
in different files share a single mechanism. A hazard arrives once the system writes its
own inferences back into the source, since those machine lines have to stay outside
identity, or annotating a hole changes it and the annotation repeats without end. A sound
design grounds identity in the human's intent scoped to its enclosing structure, drops
everything positional, keeps a second meaning-level key so equivalent intents share work,
and excludes machine-written lines from both. A developer who reformats code and loses a
mechanism has watched position leak into identity. The same intent in two files paying
full generation cost twice shows that no meaning-level key exists.

### 4. Keep a history, not a cache (Commitment History)

Treating generated code as a cache entry invites overwriting it on every change, which
discards the record of what was tried and why it was abandoned. The durable object worth
keeping is a trail of decisions, structured so that a superseded mechanism and its reason
for leaving service both remain, which a content-addressed chain of commits supports
(Merkle, 1987) and which a program understood as an accumulated theory requires (Naur,
1985). The distinction that carries weight is the fork against the step. A step is the
same approach corrected and supersedes what came before, while a fork is a materially
different approach kept in parallel because either might prove right for a different input
shape. A history also licenses an autonomous system to change its own behavior, since it
supports rolling back a poor automatic edit and showing that nothing regressed, and it is
what lets one hole be recompiled while the rest of a running program continues (Litt et
al., 2025) or a whole pipeline keep versions as it improves itself (Khattab et al., 2023).
A sound design fixes one rule for which mechanism is active when several coexist, branches
on adaptation so a correction never destroys what it corrects, and preserves every retired
mechanism with the reason it left. Inability to reconstruct from the record why a hole
produces one output today and produced another last week shows the structure has become a
cache with no history.

### 5. Make resolution an ordered choice (Resolution Choice)

Once a mechanism exists for a hole, every later call chooses among reusing it, adapting
it, and rewriting it, and reducing that choice to a cache hit or a full regeneration is
what makes naive systems thrash, since each correction then discards what the previous
mechanism learned and competence oscillates instead of accumulating. The middle option
carries the weight. Adaptation hands a mechanism its own failing case and turns a run of
failures into a converging mechanism, the same incremental refinement that self-improving
pipelines and agentic query rewriters perform when they revise a program rather than
replace it (Khattab et al., 2023; Shankar et al., 2024). The choice has to be one ordered
rule applied identically on every call, because an ad hoc choice produces nondeterminism a
developer cannot reproduce. Reuse itself stays a hypothesis until the mechanism is
confirmed against the actual input, the discipline that constrained decoding applies when
it forces output to satisfy a schema before accepting it (Willard & Louf, 2023; Scholak et
al., 2021). A sound design expresses the choice as one ordered function, defaults to
adaptation whenever a mechanism exists and fails, reserves rewrite for a changed
specification or a mechanism worth abandoning, and re-verifies every reuse on the real
input with checks ordered cheap before expensive so the common case costs almost nothing.
A hole that flips between two implementations across identical runs signals rewriting
where adaptation belonged. A hole that serves visibly stale output signals reuse without
re-verification.

### 6. Defend behavior with contracts and remembered reasons (Behavioral Contract)

The defining hazard of a system that rewrites itself is regression by omission, where a
fix for one input breaks another the new mechanism never learned about. A conventional
test suite assumes known expected outputs, and informal intent rarely supplies them, since
nothing states what a request to summarize a passage ought to return. The workable
response asserts the properties an answer must hold and the relations it must obey, a
discipline with a long lineage in design by contract (Meyer, 1992) and behavior-driven
specification (North, 2006), extended by metamorphic relations that check how an output
must change when the input is transformed (Chen et al., 1998) rather than pinning one
output. Such assertions survive a rewrite that phrases the answer differently, where a
fixed pair of input and output would raise a false alarm, and they connect to the emerging
effort to verify model-generated code against stated properties (Councilman et al., 2025).
The deeper role is memory. Carrying the reason a past decision was made into the next
rewrite, so the next generation learns that a mechanism exists because one format once
failed, keeps the system from circling back over ground it already covered, which
higher-order contracts formalize by assigning blame across the boundary a value crosses
(Findler & Felleisen, 2002). A sound design accumulates properties and relations per hole,
pins exact examples only for small canonical output spaces, feeds the reason a failed
check exists into the rewrite, and seeds each check from the current mechanism's own
behavior so it holds the moment it is written. Checks that fire on correct answers worded
differently reveal examples pinned where properties belonged. A fix that silently moved a
valued output reveals a memory too thin to defend it.

---

## Interfaces

### 7. Turn the dial one endorsed decision at a time (Gradual Formalization)

The word semi names a dial, and the human loop turns it from informal toward formal one
decision at a time, the incremental formalization that Shipman and Marshall proposed to
let people enter information loosely and structure it later, with the system suggesting
formalizations the user may accept, modify, reject, or ignore (Shipman & Marshall, 1999).
The type-theoretic form of the same dial is gradual typing, where a program moves between
dynamic and static checking one annotation at a time (Siek & Taha, 2006). The source
therefore carries two kinds of writing, the commitments a human owns and the inferences
the system proposes, kept in visibly distinct channels so authorship of any line is never
in doubt, and the machine channel stays outside the hole's identity so that annotating a
hole does not redefine it. What the system surfaces is held to a small fixed vocabulary a
human can scan, since structured reasoning traces read more legibly than generated code
alone (Chen et al., 2022; Wei et al., 2022), though a stated rationale can be causally
disconnected from the mechanism actually chosen (Jacovi & Goldberg, 2020; Turpin et al.,
2023; Lanham et al., 2023), which is why the surface serves as a prompt for human judgment
and the endorsement is what counts. The loop closes with promotion, where a human rewrites
an inference they endorse as their own commitment, which changes the intent, mints a new
identity, and raises the system's obligation, the editable-explanation move that lets a
user correct a system's account and have the correction take effect (Tian et al., 2023),
an instance of pairing human agency with automation rather than letting one replace the
other (Heer, 2019). A sound design gives human and machine disjoint channels, keeps the
machine channel identity-neutral, surfaces inferences and open decisions in a vocabulary
that earns each line, and offers one gesture that promotes an inference into a commitment.
A surface no one reads has failed to earn its lines. A promotion that fails to raise the
system's obligation shows the loop between inference and commitment is broken.

### 8. Route effects through a trusted gate (Trusted Effect Gate)

A generated mechanism is not trusted, and the stakes rise when its output is an action on
the world rather than a value, since a wrong value can be checked and discarded while a
wrong deletion cannot be recalled. Losing the ability to inspect code, as one expert put
it during the design of the paradigm, means the balance has to be tipped back by some
compensating way to trust the result. The response keeps the mechanism from acting
directly and has it describe the intended action as inspectable data that a trusted layer,
written by hand and never generated, reviews before anything takes effect, the same
reification of actions into first-class examinable objects that concept-oriented systems
adopt to keep behavior legible and interoperable (Henderson et al., 2025). That layer
rehearses the action against a faithful copy so the mechanism can branch on real state
without risk, bounds the damage before anything fires, and applies it only under approval,
which extends the precondition discipline of contracts from inputs to consequences (Meyer,
1992; Findler & Felleisen, 2002) and aligns with the effort to verify generated code
before trusting it (Councilman et al., 2025). Reversibility divides the field. For an
action with an inverse the layer captures the exact inverse at the moment of acting so
undo replays what was done instead of re-deriving it from code that may since have changed,
and for an action with no inverse the design substitutes idempotency and an explicit human
gate. A sound design routes every world-touching action through reified data and a trusted
reviewer, proves or bounds its blast radius before it fires, and records a captured inverse
for anything it means to be able to revert. An effect that fired straight from generated
code has bypassed the gate. A revert that recomputes its inverse from the current mechanism
can undo something other than what it did.

---

## Lens

### 9. Design for two readers at once (Two Users)

A semiformal system serves two audiences whose needs pull in opposite directions, the
developer who authors intent and the person who consumes the artifact the program
produces. The developer wants a surface that is live, forgiving, and promotable, the kind
of user agency malleable-software research seeks to restore (Litt et al., 2025), while the
consumer wants a mechanism that is stable, readable, and trustworthy without any knowledge
of the apparatus that produced it. The reconciling test is whether the consumer can rely
on the output while trusting nothing about the generator, which holds only when the
produced mechanism stays ordinary inspectable code carrying its own evidence of
verification, the persistent and revisable artifact that treating prompts as real program
elements demands (Liang et al., 2025; Naur, 1985) and that studies of code-generation
tools find users struggle to trust while it stays opaque (Vaithilingam et al., 2022; Barke
et al., 2022). A design that meets the developer's need for fluidity by making the output
an opaque model call has failed the consumer. A design that meets the consumer's need for
stability by freezing the developer's surface has failed the author. The lens applies to
every other guideline, since each is read once by the author while writing and once by the
consumer through the artifact it leaves behind.
